newsitem.title: FRANCE: Palestinian at meet says Israel stealing water.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian at meet says Israel stealing water.

text.p: Palestinians attending a conference on water resources said on Monday that Israel was stealing water from Arabs lands and they planned to raise the issue at the gathering of Mediterranean nations.
"We will certainly bring up what is the veritable theft of our water by the Israelis," Palestinian delegation head Professor Riyad el-Khoudary said.

"They are pumping our water from areas alongside the border with the result that about 30 percent of the water used in Israel comes from Arab sources -- mostly from Palestinian areas but also from Syria and Lebanon," he said.
Ministers and experts from Mediterranean countries on Monday began two days of discussion on water resources, an acute problem for the region of 426 million people.
Attending the meeting are representatives of all 15 European Union countries and 12 North African and Middle East states.

Delegates from both Israel and Syria attended the conference, the first such joint appearance since the election victory in May of hardline Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and subsequent rising tensions.
The two countries have waged wars in the past over control of water resources, and a common saying in the area is that the next Middle East war will not be over oil but over water.

Yoel Guilatt, deputy head of the Israeli delegation, told reporters Israel was already cooperating with Jordan on common use of water. It hoped talks with Palestinians would also aim at projects of mutual interest such as desalination plants that might help the entire region, he said.
But Khoudary complained that Israel was taking more than its fair share of water.

"In the Gaza Strip, a few thousand Israeli settlers use between five and 20 million cubic metres of water a year while the rest of the population -- a million Palestinians -- must make do with 110 million cubic metres," he said.
French government minister Jean-Claude Gaudin, opening the conference, linked a solution of the regional issue to the stability of Europe.
The European Union had been quick "to recognise that the stability and prosperity of the Mediterranean Basin are essential for Europe", he said in an opening speech.
"Water management is one of the keys to this prosperity," added Gaudin, who is France's Territorial Planning Minister and mayor of Marseille.
European delegates said they hoped to steer the conference towards technical issues but realised politics were ever present in the background.

"Everyone knows it is a fragile situation. But what the European Union, and especially France, want to do is to offer good advice on specific issues as well as the credits which everyone expects," said Pierre Roussel, head of the water department at the French Environement ministry.
